title: Behavior Coverage Atlas: know what the test proves
audience: Teams that need behavior-level evidence without turning line coverage into a correctness score.
promise: Declare named behaviors, link test receipts, distinguish assertion from execution, and keep stale, missing, failed, and duplicate evidence visible.
story: A repository-owned manifest names four product behaviors and their intended tests.
A fresh receipt separates verified assertion, execution without assertion, failed assertion, and missing evidence.
A duplicate link remains a diagnostic instead of being silently collapsed.
When the receipt target changes, historical evidence becomes stale rather than current proof.
verified_locally: Fresh four-behavior fixture with verified, weak, failed, unknown, and duplicate-link states.
Stale target run preserves historical classification across the manifest.
Source tests, lint, and package checks pass.
Current dev tests, lint, and package checks pass at revision 8c052b1.
The 1600×900 PNG preview is visually reviewed and legible at the target crop.
open_gates: Feed one behavior signal into Review Attention Map with source and freshness.
Expand parameterized and deleted-test negative fixtures.
Verify a hosted no-auth case and record external GitHub, portfolio, and Handshake readbacks.
claim_boundary: This packet proves the current dev behavior-evidence matrix and local binary preview; it does not claim complete runtime coverage, review-tool integration, hosting, or publication.
